      <title>One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <title>Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court</link>
      <description><p>A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza</p><p>Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay</a>, if the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/myanmar-rohingya-genocide-icj">court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide</a> against the Rohingya.</p><p>The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</link>
      <description><p>Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans</p><p>The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.</p><p>The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/17/egypt-eu-deal-refugees-mediterranean">promised by Ursula von der Leyen</a>, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago</p><p>Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.</p><p>Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/pete-hegseth-venezuela-nicolas-maduro-military">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Record-breaking rain lashes California’s Bay area as ‘atmospheric river’ arrives</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/18/california-atmospheric-river-flooding</link>
      <description><p>Storm expected to move into southern California, with LA residents warned of potential evacuation orders</p><p>Heavy rain pounded California’s Bay area, with record rainfall in downtown San Francisco and flooding and power outages across the region,<strong> </strong>as an “atmospheric river” arrived on Wednesday and dumped precipitation across the state.</p><p>The storm was expected to move into southern California on Wednesday night and Thursday, with Los Angeles warning residents in mudslide-prone areas of potential evacuation orders to come. Southern Californians were also warned of potential coastal flooding, heavy surf, <a href="https://www.weather.gov/lox/">wave damage to coastal piers and parking lots</a> and beach sand erosion.       <description><p>The autonomous driving company suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways days after California banned the vehicles on its own freeways</p><p>Waymo has stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US indefinitely.
